prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve animation sprite sheet. Reference is the exact cute 3D skeleton and toolbox from our game title. Make its greeting MUCH MORE READABLE. Create exactly EIGHT sequential full-figure poses in a STRICT 4-column by 2-row evenly divided grid. All eight are the SAME seated skeleton with plumed steel helmet, happy face, open toolbox on its LEFT, gears and brass trap at feet. Keep identical body, skull, helmet, toolbox, legs, ground props, size and camera between frames. Preserve softly shaded miniature 3D style, no ink cartoon switch. True clean transparent alpha background, fully transparent empty space with no gray/gold halo, shadows, noise, panels, text or floor. Each pose has clear margins.

Change ONLY the gear-holding arm to make a BIG joyful wave, not tiny wrist rotation. This is a readable greeting animation seen small at a game screen corner. The brass gear must travel by at least ONE FULL SKULL HEIGHT (about 110-140 px in each ~450px cell), from chest level to ABOVE THE HELMET. The waving arm visibly straightens and bends, wrist and forearm swing in a broad arc. One coherent arm, two arm bones, hand gripping gear; no floating gear, no extra limb. Torso and pelvis stay fixed, other hand stays near toolbox, feet and all props stay planted.

Frame0 row1 col1: gear held LOW at chest height, bent elbow by ribs, relaxed preparation. Gear BELOW eyes.
Frame1 row1 col2: forearm raises, gear level with eyes and OUTSIDE right side of head.
Frame2 row1 col3: arm extended up, gear clearly ABOVE helmet rim at its RIGHT, first high greeting extreme.
Frame3 row1 col4: hand with gear moves a full GEAR WIDTH toward LEFT over top of helmet, elbow bends naturally.
Frame4 row2 col1: hand sweeps to the RIGHT again, gear above and well outside helmet, broad greeting return.
Frame5 row2 col2: arm lowers to diagonal, gear beside face at eye height.
Frame6 row2 col3: hand comes down toward chest, intermediate lower diagonal.
Frame7 row2 col4: gear almost back to the low starting pose, smooth loop to frame0.

Draw all eight poses complete with equal scale and same lower-body registration. Leave enough transparent padding ABOVE the highest gear and around toolbox/feet. Remove the floating yellow exclamation marks from reference so the actual moving arm is clear. These are GAME ANIMATION FRAMES: pose-to-pose continuity, fixed body, and visibly LARGE arm travel are essential. Avoid copying the small raised-hand pose in every cell. No body bouncing or scaling. No other characters or scenery.
